title: Define escape-focus and contrast ramp for dense heatmap cells and row-action states
creator: Mina Chen
description: Background: During the recent accessibility sweep for dense data components we observed inconsistent focus behavior and insufficient contrast for heatmap cells and inline row actions in virtualized tables. This ticket scopes a cross-component design solution that: 1) defines a predictable "escape-focus" interaction when users exit a dense cell or inline action so keyboard flow does not get lost in virtualized DOM; 2) prescribes a contrast ramp for heatmap color tokens and a high-contrast focus treatment for actionable cells; and 3) bundles the artifacts and testing guidance required for VPAT evidence. Out of scope: full token migration across unrelated components, internationalization edge cases. Deliverables: design spec (Figma + annotated tokens), interaction spec for engineering, acceptance criteria, a VPAT evidence checklist and example screenshots, and a small demo harness for QA.
acceptance_criteria: Keyboard users can drill into a heatmap cell and activate an inline action; pressing Escape returns focus to the row start or designated logical anchor consistently across virtualized lists

Heatmap color ramp meets WCAG contrast requirements against a clearly defined background when cell has focus ring or is selected (AA for normal text target; provide rationale for data-visual exceptions)
Inline action icons/buttons (row-level) have at least 3:1 contrast relative to surrounding cell when unfocused and 4.5:1 when focused, or use dual token + outline to meet contrast on focus
Figma spec includes token names, hex values, and usage guidance; engineering has a concise interaction spec and sample code snippet for focus management
VPAT artifacts folder contains: test notes, keyboard walkthrough script, annotated screenshots, and a brief mitigation justification for heatmap semantics
Design sign-off from PM and Eng and a green QA pass on the demo harness in Chrome and VoiceOver (macOS)
tasks: Audit current heatmap and table implementations and capture failure modes (contrast, lost focus, screen reader labels)
Prototype escape-focus flow: proposals A (row-anchor), B (column-anchor), C (logical-region fallback) with keyboard walkthroughs
Define color ramp tokens for heatmap and supplementary border/outline tokens for focus states
Document recommended ARIA patterns for heatmap cells and inline actions (role attribution, aria-label strategy, aria-describedby for legends)
Create Figma frames with token variants and annotations; publish to design system library
Collaborate with ENG to implement a small demo harness (virtualized table + heatmap) and a test script for QA
Assemble VPAT evidence pack and attach to this ticket
decisions: Use row-anchor escape-focus as default because it aligns with keyboard mental model for tabular data and minimizes DOM mutations in virtualization
Introduce a thin high-contrast focus outline token (focus-ring-compact) instead of increasing base fill contrast for heatmap cells to preserve data encoding
Expose an opt-in aria-mode on Heatmap component for strict data-visual semantics vs. interactive-cell semantics to support both read-only and interactive workflows
review_feedback: PM (Rohan Gupta): ensure change does not regress automated snapshot-driven visual tests for dashboards
Eng (Lukas Becker): avoid DOM reordering; prefer focus restoration to an anchor element outside the virtualized window
Accessibility consultant (external): suggest adding live-region announcements when a cell action completes to help screen reader users
qa_plan: Run keyboard walkthrough script across Chrome + NVDA and Safari + VoiceOver; record video evidence
Verify contrast ratios with the design tokens applied in storybook examples at 100% and 200% zoom
Run automated axe-core checks on the demo harness and triage violations that are beyond intended visual semantics
Cross-check VPAT checklist items and attach signed evidence to the artifacts folder
roll_out_plan: Merge prototype behind a feature flag; ship to internal Canary environment
Run a 2-week accessibility pilot with the Platform team and gather regression metrics
After sign-off, promote tokens to the design system release and include migration notes
Publish VPAT evidence as part of the 2026 Q1 accessibility package for enterprise customers
